records.text: A cockroach is a small critter found across Northrend.

Highlord Tirion Fordring leads the Argent Crusade's struggle against the Lich King and recruits volunteers despite Horde–Alliance division. He assesses Arthas's attacks and seeks to strengthen the defenses, admitting that the Lich King's response can be faster than he anticipates. In addressing the death knight Darion, he insists on honor: victory gained by sinking to the Scourge's methods would make the Crusade no better than its enemy.
Onslaught Paladins are armed members of the Onslaught encountered in Icecrown. They answer an attack with Shield Charge, bringing their martial training directly into the fight.
An Onslaught guard stationed at the harbor, this infantry fighter uses a ranged shot when combat begins.
An Onslaught gryphon rider over the harbor, armed to throw spears in combat. Uzo Deathcaller sends adventurers to bring down these riders in his No Fly Zone assignment.
An Onslaught Raven Bishop who calls a raven flock in combat and casts a healing spell when badly wounded, supporting the force around the harbor.

Baron Sliver directs Ebon Blade operations at the Shadow Vault, where his death knights are fighting the Scourge. He sends allies on urgent assignments, including demoralizing the vrykul with his men’s banners and recovering death knights taken captive. His dry chuckle accompanies a reminder that the vault is barely holding; he treats pressure on the vrykul as a continuing priority.

Lord-Commander Arete is a death knight commander at Death's Rise, pursuing the Scarlet Onslaught and the whereabouts of Grand Admiral Westwind. He regards the Scarlets as an enemy that must be ended, even when the Argent Crusade tolerates their presence. His campaign includes interrogating their officers and seeking answers from Archbishop Landgren's spirit; news that the Scarlets were deceived by Mal'Ganis draws an amused, gleeful reaction.

Ravenous Jaws is a hostile beast found in the Death's Rise region. Its name applies to a creature population with many spawns, rather than evidence of one individualized character; it attacks with Thrash.

Setaal Darkmender is a draenei death knight at Death's Rise, marked by cold, sly hostility toward the Scarlet Onslaught. She wants their dead transformed into the kind of beings they despise, and gives a tincture for raising them as undead. Her vengeance is personal in tone, and she frames the plan as repayment for the Scarlets' torture, zealotry, and murder.

At Death’s Rise, Uzo Deathcaller performs a blood ritual to turn a captured Onslaught gryphon into a bone gryphon, then urges its use against the Scarlet Onslaught’s riders at Onslaught Harbor. His instructions frame the flying patrols as a continuing problem: he says he needs the task done each day, and his quest dialogue points out that the riders are still flying. He hopes the player will return for another sortie.

At Death’s Rise, Aurochs Grimbane seeks current intelligence on the Scarlet Onslaught’s plans. He sends the player to search baggage trunks at Onslaught Harbor for documents, describing the player as his instrument in the task. Aurochs says the Onslaught changes its plans daily; he will sift through the documents for anything actionable and may call on the player again.

Captain Welsington is one of the captains Lord-Commander Arete identifies at Onslaught Harbor while seeking the hidden grand admiral. When pressed for information, Welsington cries that Archbishop Landgren must know. His recorded line offers a lead toward the admiral’s whereabouts, rather than claiming Welsington knows the answer himself.

Captain Hartford is one of the captains Lord-Commander Arete identifies at Onslaught Harbor as a possible source of information about the hidden grand admiral. Hartford’s final line denies knowing where the admiral is and ends with a defiant insult.
A dead vrykul at Death's Rise.
Setaal's Pet is a ghoul companion associated with the Darkmender.

Archbishop Landgren has been resurrected and promoted as an archbishop within the Crimson Cathedral. Defiant about being killed again, he warns that he will not die so quickly this time and fights with Mind Blast. Arete seeks information about Grand Admiral Westwind from Landgren's compelled soul.

Lord-Commander Arete is adept at nullifying magic and wants Grand Admiral Westwind dealt with. He equips the player to counter Westwind's protective sphere, then questions the resurrected Archbishop Landgren about Westwind's location, threatening to destroy Landgren's soul when he refuses. Arete's dialogue treats the captive as a tool once the Hidden Hollow lead is revealed.

Onslaught Darkweavers are elite adversaries whose battle cries promise death and claim they will feast on a victim's soul. One warns that even death offers no escape, casting these recurring foes as soul-hunters who expect their victims to remain within their reach.

Grand Admiral Westwind leads the Scarlet Onslaught and keeps himself secluded on Northrend. A note attributed to him promises that the Onslaught will overcome the Lich King and bring order to Azeroth. He relies on a magical sphere for protection, but vows revenge on both the Lich King and the player when that defense fails.
Bone Gryphons are undead gryphons.
A captured spy at Death's Rise.
An Onslaught destrier, a horse associated with the Scarlet Onslaught.
A Shadow Cultist of the Cult of the Damned who casts Shadowform on appearing and uses Mind Sear in combat.
A morbid carcass classified as undead that attacks with Cleave.
Vault Geist is a geist. When aggroed, it leaps to a position, giving it a sudden, mobile attack pattern.
Rabid Cannibal is a humanoid attacker whose combat behavior includes a Carnivorous Bite.
The Death Knight Master is a humanoid combatant who attacks with Plague Strike.
Known as The Ocular, this solitary, powerful figure attacks with Deathly Stare.

Vile speaks in blunt, violent bursts, promising to crush, maim, and destroy. Vile also asks if they are free and warmly addresses the player, hinting at a concern for freedom and an unusual shift in attitude.

Lady Nightswood challenges intruders during her ritual and demands to know where Baron Sliver is, saying she would have words with him. She seeks him out, though the reason for their confrontation is unknown.

At the Shadow Vault, Baron Sliver secretly aids the Ebon Blade while pretending to remain under the Lich King's control; he warns visitors to stay out of sight. Formerly in the Lich King's employ, he knows Sovereign Rods can control intelligent Scourge and is assembling a modified one to turn the Vault's undead against their master. He also seeks to take the Vault and blind the Lich King by destroying The Ocular.

The Leaper is a Scourge creature at the Shadow Vault whose corpse Baron Sliver identifies as a potential weapon against the Lich King. Sliver proposes using a Sovereign Rod to break its control and turn it against its former master. Its vocalizations are garbled cries.

A vrykul warrior of Jotunheim, this fighter meets opponents with blunt threats, calling them sniveling pigs and promising death or to feed them to dogs. Vile urges the player to kill vrykul across the region, placing this warrior among the foes encountered in the Shadow Vault campaign.

Instructor Hroegar is a named individual whom Vaelen the Flayed identifies as wearing the key to Vaelen’s chains outside Ufrang’s Hall. He also yields Vrykul bones required by a separate task in Jotunheim, making him a target in more than one local errand.

Thane Ufrang is a patient vrykul strategist who bides his time in the war at Jotunheim. When a messenger orders him to stand down in Duke Lankral's name, Ufrang rejects the command with threats and vows to feed the messenger to dogs.

Duke Lankral leads the Ebon Blade campaign against the vrykul of Jotunheim. He seeks to weaken their resolve by turning their trials into a source of Scourged Vargul rather than Ymirjar, and by burning their banners. He prizes strategic advantage over moral restraint and treats the player's successes as gains for the fight against the Lich King.

Mjordin Combatants are vrykul warriors who spar on the Savage Ledge under their thane's men. They taunt challengers and treat combat as entertainment; one says killing the challenger will not bring him closer to proving himself at Valhalas.

Vaelen the Flayed is a captured death knight who says his entire contingent was taken by the vrykul. He regrets failing to recognize the trap that led to their capture, then dryly warns others not to share his fate. His shackles still bind him, and he asks for the key held by Instructor Hroegar; he says he will handle the key himself.
Initiate Claget serves as a blades vendor in the Shadow Vault area, where visitors can browse his goods.
Initiate Roderick is a Shadow Vault vendor whose trade is poisons and reagents. Visitors can browse his goods.
Initiate Gahark is a Shadow Vault vendor for general goods. Visitors can browse his wares.

The Leaper is a one-eyed geist whose speech can be hard to follow until he clears his throat. He works against the Lich King's forces, urging the humiliation of vrykul champions and turning Jotunheim's harpoon defenses on its proto-drakes. His unnerving cackle and piercing stare make him theatrical as well as calculating.

Efrem the Faithful is an ambitious former Scarlet Onslaught member who says he left to pursue distinction and means to prove himself to the Lich King. His words are blunt and hostile, and he meets challengers with the same fierce confidence he brings to his bid for the Lich King's favor.

Sigrid Iceborn is a vrykul contender who expects to rise by defeating her rivals and earning a place in the Lich King's service. She dismisses other fighters as inept, bristles at anyone who doubts vrykul women's ability, and treats a loss as temporary: she promises to return better prepared.

Tinky Wickwhistle is a sharp-tongued competitor at Savage Ledge, openly dismissive of the Lich King's trial by combat. He threatens opponents with a kneecapping, celebrates with a shout, and uses a wrench and dynamite. He says a teleport accident brought him here and boasts that he has moved up in the world, contrasting himself with his more earnest Borean Tundra duplicate.

Onu'zun is a challenger who speaks of himself in the third person. He has come to test himself against the vrykul, rise through Valhalas, and earn a place working for the Lich King if he wins. His blunt threat to kill opponents dead suits his ambitious, combative outlook.

An Ebon Blade death knight captured by the vrykul and held in a cage in Jotunheim. Vaelen identifies the prisoners as his men and says their return is needed to help hold the line against the Lich King's forces.
Mirador is a named beast in the Savage Ledge area.
An elite humanoid combatant identified as an Argent Champion, serving among the Argent forces.
An elite humanoid combatant known as a Crusader of Virtue, bearing a name that marks a crusader's martial role.
An Ebon Blade prisoner held in the Scourgeholme area of Icecrown.
An Ebon Blade prisoner held in Scourgeholme who voices a promise of revenge for another time. The words suggest defiance, though they do not identify a target or explain what provoked the grievance.
An Ebon Blade prisoner held among Scourgeholme's captives in Icecrown.

A reanimated Crusader in Scourgeholme, one of the undead targets in the Argent Crusade's purge. Being struck by Sprinkle Holy Water triggers a Freed Crusader Soul spell, hinting at the captive soldier beneath the Scourge's control.
A Forgotten Depths High Priest among the forces targeted in the Argent Crusade's Scourgeholme purge. In battle, this priest casts Encasing Webs and Mind Sear.
An acolyte of Forgotten Depths in the Scourgeholme area. The title places this figure in a junior religious role.
A beast called a Carrion Fleshstripper, part of the creature population around Scourgeholme in Icecrown. Its name suggests a scavenger.

Vile is an excitable abomination at the Shadow Vault who speaks in the third person and delights in fire and proto-drakes. He recruits help against the vrykul around Jotunheim, including setting their buildings alight with a stolen proto-drake.

Vaelen the Flayed is an Ebon Blade death knight at the Shadow Vault who has returned to recover his captured men. He says the Lich King's forces are close to breaking through and that the defenders can barely hold without the imprisoned death knights. He urgently asks for their release.

Crusade Commander Entari leads Argent Crusade efforts from the Argent Vanguard. After the assault on Scourgeholme was beaten back, he seeks help freeing crusaders whom the Scourge use as living shields, and remains concerned for soldiers still stranded in the field and at Scourgeholme.

Crusader Lord Dalfors serves at the Argent Vanguard, where he urges the defense against Forgotten Depths Nerubians pouring through the breach. His grim reaction to their seemingly endless numbers reflects the pressure on the crusaders holding the line.
Crusader Sunborn is a crusader at the Argent Vanguard who remembers Eversong Woods before Arthas cut through it. Sunborn's thoughts linger on the beauty of the land before that devastation.

Father Gustav works at the Argent Vanguard to find a cure for the toxin afflicting its injured soldiers. He asks for Forgotten Depths venom glands so he can test them, hoping to counter a poison the crusaders have only managed to slow.

Penumbrius is a bronze dragon who takes mortal form to live and communicate among mortals. An ally of the Argent Crusade and caretaker of the proto-brood, he offers his kin's aid in the fight against the Lich King and helps the crusaders seek survivors at Scourgeholme.

The Bone Witch is a banshee inhabiting a vrykul in Njorndar Village. She remembers a home in Quel’Thalas, a husband and children, and blames the Lich King for taking her family and life. Unable to strike him directly, she vows threefold revenge. She offers to teach temporary possession of water terrors to attack Jotunheim’s vrykul, and casts bones to invite a helper to choose their fate.
Glory is an undead.
An injured crusader in Icecrown.
A Njorndar Spear-Sister is a vrykul fighter who threatens to gut intruders and feed them to dogs.
A Valhalas Vargul is a vrykul foe in Jotunheim. It attacks nearby enemies with Cleave and its death counts toward the Bone Witch's plan to use a Water Terror against the vrykul.
A webbed crusader found in Jotunheim. When it dies, it summons a Forgotten Depths Ambusher.
A Njorndar proto-drake, a beast.
A webbed crusader found in Jotunheim. When it dies, it summons a Freed Crusader and grants credit for Scourge Tactics.
Imhadria is a named stable master. Her greeting describes help with recovering lost companions, and her stablemaster role connects her with pet stabling.
Bileblow is a named undead figure identified as a poisons vendor.
Sarhule the Risen is a named undead figure identified as a reagent vendor.
Initiate Brenners is identified as an innkeeper.
Shambles is a named undead figure identified as a food and drink vendor.
Boltskull is a named undead figure identified as a general goods vendor.
Mangled sells trade supplies to visitors who come to browse his goods.
A Shadow Vault Boneguard is an elite humanoid fighter among the vault's ranks.
Morlia Doomwing is a flight master who helps travelers journey quickly. When attacked, Morlia calls an enraged gryphon and an enraged wyvern to her aid.
Rotclaw is Imhadria's pet, a beast kept under her care.
Jotunheim Proto-Drakes carry riders as part of Jotunheim's aerial defenses. The Leaper seeks to turn the defenders' own harpoon guns against them.
A Forgotten Depths Slayer is an undead combatant of the Forgotten Depths.
An undead gryphon known as a Shadow Vault Gryphon.
Runesmith Balehammer sells blacksmithing supplies and repairs equipment in Northrend.

The Ebon Watcher warns the Highlord that the Lich King holds the consciousness of cunning, intelligent, and ruthless individuals. It cautions that the Highlord is now on the Lich King’s domain and says victory is impossible under the present circumstances.
Iydallus is an undead figure associated with the Ebon Watch.

Nergeld is Dr. Terrible’s massive flesh-giant prototype for an ultimate weapon. A quest uses the construct as a controllable weapon; its recorded lines describe it coming to life and an enemy falling apart.

Once the champion of Thane Ufrang, Bethod Feigr says Thane Illskar sabotaged him with dark magic during his bid for ascendance in Valhalas, leaving him in his present state. He seeks vengeance, yet speaks of shame and warns visitors to leave before he loses control.
An Argent Crusader captured by the Scourge, this soldier urges a quick escape and warns of an impending attack while being rescued from Scourgeholme.

Apprentice Osterkilgr serves Dr. Terrible and guards the doctor's plans for Nergeld, a flesh giant made from vargul. He boasts that a legion of these creations will destroy his opponents and threatens death to anyone seeking the plans.
A sentry worg found in Scourgeholme, this beast attacks intruders with Tendon Rip.
Veteran Crusader Aliocha Segard is an Argent Crusade quartermaster who offers the order's goods to visitors.
Aedan Moran is a flight master who offers fast travel.
Durik Bronzebomb is an engineering supplies vendor.
Halig Fireforge supplies blacksmithing goods.
Crusader Marisse is an ammunition supplier. The title Crusader and her ammunition specialty distinguish her service among the area's vendors.
Supply Officer Thalmers handles poisons, reagents and trade supplies.
Sister Colleen Tulley is the area's food and drink vendor, a distinct provision service among the nearby suppliers.
The Lich King is an undead.

Thane Illskar accepts a challenge issued with Bethod Feigr’s sword at the Circle of Suffering, sending his champions Volgur and Brita against the challenger first. He boasts that he is beyond his defeated champions and threatens a quick death. Bethod accuses him of sabotaging his fight for ascendance in Valhalas with dark magic.
Volgur fights with Demoralize, Chop, Charge and Whirlwind.
Brita is a humanoid who attacks players.
An Argent Skytalon is a dragonkin in Icecrown.
A Forgotten Depths Underking is an undead Scourge combatant at Scourgeholme, listed among the forces the Ebon Watcher asks the player to destroy.
A Forgotten Depths High Priest is an undead Scourge combatant at Scourgeholme, listed among the forces the Ebon Watcher asks the player to destroy. In combat, it casts Encasing Webs.
A Forgotten Depths Underking is an undead creature found in Icecrown.

Crusader Bridenbrad is an individual crusader stricken with the plague of undeath. He refuses to return to safety because he fears exposing others, and dreads being raised to serve Arthas. Though he has only hours left, he remains grateful to those who help him and proud to have served beside Tirion Fordring; he hopes the land will be freed from Arthas.

The Ebon Watcher speaks as a former servant of the Lich King, freed with his knights at Light's Hope. He presents aid to the Argent Crusade as repayment to Highlord Tirion Fordring, while stressing that the Ebon Blade's methods and future differ from the Crusade's; he describes their help in Icecrown as a debt to be paid before they part ways.
An undead ghoul that attacks with jagged spikes and claw slashes.

Arch Druid Lilliandra is a druid associated with the Argent Vanguard who greets heroes warmly. Tirion's request directs a hero to seek her help reaching Moonglade and ask Keeper Remulos to aid Bridenbrad; a recorded exchange shows her offering a portal to Moonglade.

At Blackwatch, Darkrider Arly treats the Fleshwerks as a major threat and pushes for intelligence to disrupt its production. She resents the time spent recovering Olakin, saying one crusader is much like another to her even as she recognizes the Argents value their commander. Her blunt call for Olakin to get back to work fits her unsentimental, work-first manner.
Mjordin Water Magi are hostile spellcasters who threaten intruders with death and even promise to eat their hearts. They cast Summon Water Terror.
A Water Terror is an elemental summoned by a Mjordin Water Magus.
Rhydian, a Kirin Tor associate, politely says he overheard a conversation and offers to help, showing attentiveness and a willingness to assist.

Siegemaster Fezzik organizes the defense at the Argent Vanguard, directing recruits to man the tower cannons against the Scourge and its frost wyrms. He praises those who help save the base, but the battle weighs on him: he says the screams of the dying will haunt him forever, even as urgency leaves little time for instructions.
The Forgotten Depths Slayer is a common creature found around the Argent Vanguard.
The Frostbrood Destroyer is a creature found around the Argent Vanguard.
The Argent Champion is a humanoid found around the Argent Vanguard.

Highlord Tirion Fordring directs the Argent Crusade's advance into Icecrown, seeking the Ebon Watcher's knowledge for an assault on Scourgeholme. He warns against losing focus after victory, yet recognizes his soldiers' need for respite and values allies' contributions. He entrusts a blessed Crusade banner to cleanse the ground at Crusaders' Pinnacle, where the Scourge have piled the skulls of fallen crusaders, and urges courage against the coming resistance.

Father Gustav is a leader in the Argent Crusade’s Icecrown campaign who treats its fallen as souls needing release: he asks the player to use holy water on reanimated crusaders so their spirits may be freed. He has chosen a site for Justice Keep and sends his report to Highlord Tirion before the crusade continues its advance. His words describe freeing the dead as a grim duty that must be done.

Crusade Architect Silas is helping turn Scourgeholme into Justice Keep, a fortress intended to rise from the ruined landscape. His rebuilding plan begins with a stone that can resist decay: he sends the search to Crystalsong for disease-resistant heartwood and protective elven masonry.
A skeletal constructor active in Icecrown, this Scourge-made construct shields itself with bone armour and attacks with shadow bolt.
A chained abomination found in Icecrown, it fights with heavy cleaving attacks when engaged.
A corpulent horror found in Icecrown, it attacks targets at a distance with a Scourge Hook.

Morbidus is a flesh giant and the Fleshwerks' greatest accomplishment. The Shadow Vault sends Margrave Dhakar with reinforcements to begin the assault; Dhakar orders his forces into battle when the attack is ready.
A Vile Creeper is a creature found in two Icecrown areas.

Crusader Olakin Sainrith is a crusader at Blackwatch who investigates the Scourge’s use of metal in its forces. He regards the fallen defenders as heroes who deserve rest, and sees burning their repurposed corpses as a grim but necessary way to honor them and protect the living.

Crusade Engineer Spitzpatrick is preparing a bomber that needs crystallized energy for fuel. He warns that the magically charged creatures of the Unbound Thicket hold enough energy to kill everyone if it destabilizes, while treating their destruction as a grim necessity for the project.
Slumbering Mjordin are vrykul held in magical sleep in the Halls of the Ancestors. The Bone Witch seeks Iskalder among the sleepers and directs an adventurer to wake them.

Jotunheim Sleep-Watchers are hostile watchers stationed among the sleeping mjordin in the Halls of the Ancestors. They meet intruders with threats and contemptuous insults, then strike at close range.
Zarod is an undead master summoner.
A Kul’galar Oracle holds an oracle role among the Kul’galar.

Salranax the Flesh Render is an undead lord of Scourgeholme. The Ebon Watcher identifies him as ruling over its first-tier temple and names him alongside High Priest Yath’amon and Underking Talonox as formidable opponents whose defeat could loosen the Scourge’s hold.

Underking Talonox holds court at the Pit of Fiends, where the Ebon Watcher identifies him as one of Scourgeholme’s lords. The Watcher calls these foes formidable and says Acherus death knights can answer a war horn for aid. Talonox responds to that horn and fights with Mandible Crush.

High Priest Yath'amon preaches at the spirit tower on Scourgeholme’s second tier and is named among the lords the Ebon Watcher urges challengers to defeat. The Watcher describes them as formidable and offers a war horn to call Acherus death knights for aid. Yath'amon responds to the horn and attacks with Venomous Bite.
The Lithe Stalker is an undead creature that follows the unit whose spell hits it.

The Lumbering Atrocity speaks to a “little geist” in short, simple phrases. It asks whether the geist wants a present, wonders what the bomb is for, offers to deliver it, and says it is unsure the bomb is safe. Its words show concern about the delivery and the geist’s safety.
The Skeletal Runesmith is an undead combatant identified by its runesmith title. In battle, it uses Pierce Armor.

Umbral Brutes are undead enemies at Malykriss. Vereth uses them in a sabotage scheme: a controlled Lithe Stalker throws rocks at them to provoke fights with lesser undead and disrupt production. Their recorded battle cries react to being pelted and anger, giving these combatants a forceful voice.

Vereth the Cunning is an Ebon Blade agent at the Rise of Suffering, directing efforts against death knights still loyal to Arthas at Malykriss. His assignments use controlled Lithe Stalkers to scout the citadel and provoke fights among its undead workforce, reflecting his preference for reconnaissance and sabotage. He regards Arthas's pride as a weakness and expects the Ebon Blade will have its chance to strike.

Keritose Bloodblade is based at the Shadow Vault, where he prepares an assault on the Scourge’s saronite quarry. He wants its defenses and lookouts weakened, worries that its crystals could threaten his gryphons, and uses a shade to get close to plaguehounds. His dry remark that Arthas is “not used to losing” follows evidence that the Vile Hold is active again.
An Eidolon Watcher is a shade used in Keritose’s operations against the Scourge quarry. He directs its use to feed the starving plaguehounds and destroy their defensive crystals.
Risen Laborers are undead workers in the Shadow Vault region.
Restless Lookouts are ghouls watching the Scourge quarry. Keritose considers them fragile and directs the player to thin their ranks before the coming assault.
An undead plaguehound.
Baelok is the Rider of Blood, a named and powerful undead combatant. He uses Death Grip and Draw Soul in combat and can summon a dancing runeblade.
Rokir is the Rider of the Unholy, a named and powerful undead combatant. In battle he calls a Zombie Horde and casts Death and Decay.
Sapph, the Rider of Frost, is an undead combatant who welcomes others to the world of the unliving. He says he expected the listener, praises their fighting, and uses Chains of Ice in battle.
A Death Knight Initiate of the Host of Suffering, found among other initiates in the same area.
A Death Knight Initiate of the Host of Suffering, found among other initiates in the same area.
An undead soldier known as a Risen Soldier.
An undead soldier known as a Summoned Soldier.
The Scourgebeak Fleshripper is an undead creature found in the Fleshwerks region of Icecrown.
Patches is a ghoul creation held in chains by Doctor Sabnok in the Sanctum of Reanimation. He wants revenge on the doctor and says he will no longer be cut open or sewn up.

Iceskin Sentries are gargoyles found resting as stone on the eastern and southern walls inside the Rise of Suffering. Gargoyles serve as scouts, but their heavy bodies need long periods of stone rest to conserve energy for flight. A Lithe Stalker's heave can strike them while they sleep.
The Lich King commands his creations to leave no survivors and feast on the living. He seeks to intimidate opponents into laying down their arms and surrendering their souls.
A Crusader of Virtue whose words are warm and grateful: they thank the listener, welcome them, and cheer the hero of the Vanguard. The lines give this crusader a generous, appreciative manner.
A high priest of the Forgotten Depths, an undead presence encountered in Icecrown's depths. In combat this priest uses Encasing Webs and Mind Sear. The title marks a religious role.
The Forgotten Depths Underking is an undead figure encountered in the depths of Icecrown. The title gives this figure a distinctive place among the named inhabitants of the Forgotten Depths.
A Wrathstrike Gargoyle, an undead gargoyle encountered in the Forgotten Depths of Icecrown. Its name marks a distinct kind of creature.
A Death Knight Adept bearing the designation Host of Suffering, encountered in Icecrown. The title identifies a death knight in an advanced role.
A reanimated crusader encountered in the Forgotten Depths of Icecrown. The name identifies this figure as a fallen crusader returned to undeath.

Highlord Tirion Fordring honors Crusader Bridenbrad’s valor and refuses to abandon him to undeath, urgently seeking help from Keeper Remulos and A’dal. He believes an artifact reported to be Arthas Menethil’s heart might preserve his remaining humanity, offering a chance of redemption. He plans to approach it disguised as a cultist.
Mirador is a beast in Northrend.
A humanoid crusade commander named Entari.
Crusader Lord Dalfors is a humanoid crusader.
Crusader Sunborn is a humanoid crusader.
Penumbrius is a dragonkin flight master who offers travel assistance.
An Argent Skytalon, a dragonkin.
Dreadwind is an undead flight master who asks travelers where they wish to fly.
Quartermaster Vaskess provides supplies and brusquely asks visitors to make their requests quickly.

A festering corpse in the Scourge's Fleshwerks. Crusader Olakin Sainrith describes the fallen dead as heroes the Scourge raises or uses to build abominations, and calls for these corpses to be burned. The corpse responds to Olakin's Torch.

A Scourge containment crystal scattered through the base. Keritose Bloodblade suspects the crystals are defensive structures and sends an eidolon watcher to destroy them, hoping to weaken Scourge defenses while investigating the saronite quarry. A spell hit grants monster credit and causes the crystal to despawn.

Geirrvif is a val'kyr who offers challengers matches in Valhalas, the vrykul battle pit. She warns that its contests can be deadly and insists that combatants stay within the ring. She regards fallen opponents as unworthy and treats the arena's succession of challengers as a test of skill and honor.
A Pustulent Horror is a large, hostile creature found in Icecrown. These horrors are encountered in groups across two local areas.

A hulking abomination stands among the Lich King's defenses at the Broken Front. Koltira identifies it as one of the enemy minions to be defeated while probing the defenses around the first gate. On death, it casts Exploding Corpse.
Icy Ghouls are encountered across the Broken Front and the neighboring battlefield area.

A Shadow Adept of the Cult of the Damned is one of the Lich King's minions at the Broken Front, where Koltira directs the attack against the citadel's defenses. The adept casts a Green Cultist Beam while out of combat, marking a distinct cultist presence among those defenses.
Vicious Geists appear around the Broken Front and its neighboring battlefield area.
Plagued Fiends are found in two areas around the Broken Front. In combat, they cast Plague Bite.
Undying Minions are encountered across the Broken Front and its neighboring battlefield area. In combat, they cast Necrotic Strike.

Gjonner the Merciless is a vrykul death knight who oversees challenges at Valhalas. He greets challengers with contempt, spits at them, and calls even a hard-won victory unimpressive beside what awaits in the next match. He threatens to summon ghouls and warns successful fighters that their next opponent may kill them.

An undead necromancer among the enemy forces at the Broken Front. Thassarian identifies Malefic Necromancers as one of three enemy groups to study for weaknesses before the assault on Icecrown's gates. This one uses Bone Armor.

Baelok, the Rider of Blood, is a vrykul who rose through the ranks largely by brutality, according to Vereth the Cunning. Vereth warns that Baelok can steal life force, advising challengers to keep their distance and hinder that ability. Baelok also uses Death Grip and Draw Soul in combat.

Rokir, the Rider of the Unholy, is a death knight whom Vereth says he served beside. Vereth describes him as especially skilled in unholy arts and ruthless; in combat, Rokir commands undead minions and uses Plague Strike and Death and Decay.

Sapph, the Rider of Frost, is a death knight whose sweet manner masks lethal intent, according to Vereth, who warns that she lulls victims before unleashing frost attacks. In her own words she greets challengers with confidence, welcomes them to the world of the unliving, and praises a worthy fight; she also uses Chains of Ice.
Icefury is Sapph's undead steed, a named creature found in the same Icecrown region.
An unnamed Alliance soldier who has been slain. Many such fallen soldiers are found across two areas of Icecrown.

Koltira Deathweaver and Thassarian both describe Coprous the Defiled as a powerful zombie at the Death Gate in Mord'rethar and ask for a weakness to exploit. In combat he uses Acid Geyser and knockdown.

Risen Alliance Soldier is an undead battlefield foe among the Scourge targeted by Argent Tournament field training. Avareth Swiftstrike’s quest frames those encounters as a chance for competitors to keep honing their skills while learning mounted combat. Its name identifies a risen soldier of the Alliance, giving this enemy a military identity amid the wider Scourge.
Bloodsunder is identified as Baelok's steed.
Bloodsunder is identified as Baelok's steed.
Icefury is identified as Sapph's steed.
Plaguehoof is identified as Rokir's steed.

Lumbering Atrocity is a Scourge opponent targeted by Argent Tournament field training. Avareth Swiftstrike and Amariel Sunsworn each give competitors an exercise in practicing against the Scourge while learning mounted combat, and this creature is a credited target in both. Its name presents it as a lumbering monster on Icecrown’s battlefield.

Matthias Lehner warns that an unnamed pursuer will come after someone who disturbed something, and urges them to hide with Faceless One blood. He later points them through a portal to the surface, warning that the pursuer will keep searching. His urgent warnings suggest he knows the danger firsthand.

Warlord Hork Strongbrow is a mortally wounded Horde fighter rescued from the Broken Front by the Argent Crusade. He recalls battling Alliance and Scourge alike and accepts that his time is over. Before dying, he asks a passing soldier to carry word to Sky-Reaver Korm Blackscar that he died fighting for the Horde.

Marshal Ivalius is a mortally wounded Alliance soldier rescued from the Broken Front by the Argent Crusade. Remembering the battle's relentless slaughter, he asks a passing soldier to tell his commander, High Captain Justin Bartlett, that he died a soldier of the Alliance.
An invisible stalker associated with oozes in Icecrown.
An Ebon Blade defender associated with the order's presence in Icecrown.
An undead combatant called a Shadow Vault Skirmisher, found in the Shadow Vault area.
The Lordaeron footsoldier is holding a position against an undead assault and warns that a prince has gone mad. The repeated alarm and resolve convey a soldier focused on the immediate defense.
An elite saronite shaper encountered in Icecrown, this formidable combatant relies on a War Stomp in battle.
An Ebon Blade Winged Defender encountered around the Shadow Vault, this humanoid is defined by its defensive post and winged role.

A Ymirheim Chosen Warrior, one of the Ymirjar favored by the Lich King and based in their city. It threatens outsiders with gutting them and eating their hearts, matching the brutal challenge posed by the Chosen.
A Blight Falconer encountered in Ymirheim, fighting as a combatant with ranged shots.
An undead carrion hunter prowls the Broken Front region. Its name describes a scavenging predator.
A savage proto-drake in the Broken Front region, this beast attacks with flame breath.
An undead assaulter found in the Shadow Vault area. Its title marks it as an attacker.
A humanoid Ymirjar element shaper in the Broken Front region, it uses Avalanche and Torn Earth in combat.

A wounded Horde berserker at the Broken Front, he says he is finished and urges the player to kill the Dying Soldiers in revenge against the Alliance's wounded. He asks for this in the Horde's name; the quest sends the player to report to Sky-Reaver Korm Blackscar.

Father Kamaros is a Light-devoted survivor in Scourge-held Icecrown, too weak to escape alone. He asks for help reaching safety and hopes to fight the Scourge again. His gratitude and concern for his brothers and comrades shape his appeal: he wants them told he lives and plans to return to them.
The Ymirheim Spear Gun is an automated weapon emplacement in Ymirheim, and it casts Launch Spear outside combat.

Orbaz Bloodbane, the Hand of Suffering, is the leader of the Host of Suffering and serves the Lich King. He meets Ebon Blade challengers with mockery, boasts of the power the Lich King gave him, and threatens to extinguish every last one of them. His words frame the encounter as a final fight.

A Dying Soldier lies wounded among the combatants of the Broken Front, one of many such soldiers there. He says the Scourge taunt the dying and begs for an end to his torment and mercy for his companions. His brief reply describes himself as finished and beyond help.
Margrave Dhakar is a named Ebon Blade commander who rallies the Knights for battle at the Fleshwerks. His dialogue also condemns the works as a source of soldiers for the Lich King's armies.
An Ebon Blade Veteran represents the order's experienced fighting ranks. The name marks this as a veteran role rather than an individually named figure.
An Ebon Blade Reaper serves among the order's combatants.
An Umbral Brute is a hulking creature that protests when struck by a thrown rock, then attacks. Its outbursts boast about crushing the one who provoked it.
A Skeletal Runesmith is a skeletal combatant that uses Pierce Armor in a fight, bringing runic craft to its attacks.
A Saronite Shaper is a formidable combatant whose title suggests a connection to saronite; it uses War Stomp in a fight.
An undead creature identified as a Lithe Stalker.
An undead creature identified as an Iceskin Sentry.
An undead Death Knight Adept bearing the Host of Suffering designation.
An undead Death Knight Initiate bearing the Host of Suffering designation.
An undead Death Knight Initiate bearing the Host of Suffering designation.
A Val'kyr Taskmistress who uses Touch of the Val'kyr in combat.

Saronite Mine Slaves are workers trapped in the mine, and the saronite has left this one hearing voices and believing its purpose lies below. Its speech shifts between urging others to flee, insisting it must obey, and asking to be freed. It warns that something in the saronite and rocks is speaking in their minds.
Foreman Thaldrin is a named humanoid with the title of foreman.
This Hulking Horror is an undead creature targeted in Captain Kendall's effort to secure the Icecrown Citadel area for a saronite-bomb detonation. In combat, it uses Infected Bite.
This Hulking Horror is an undead creature targeted in Sergeant Kregga's effort to control Scourge defenses before a saronite-bomb strike. In combat, it uses Infected Bite.
A Valiance Commando is a humanoid with a commando role in the Icecrown Citadel area.
The Shadow Vault Abomination is an undead abomination.

Sergeant Kregga is a woman leading the attack below Icecrown Citadel. She asks for help suppressing Scourge defenses and moving the assault forward with saronite bombs, including lighting their fuse. Koltira has recommended the player to her.

Captain Kendall leads troops sent below Icecrown Citadel to exploit a structural weakness with borrowed saronite bombs. The operation aims to weaken Scourge forces; Kendall plans to evacuate the men before detonation. Kendall greets a living friend of Thassarian with dry humor about the company Thassarian keeps.
A restless lookout keeps watch in the Weeping Quarry.
A risen laborer among the undead targeted in the Weeping Quarry assault.
A hungering plaguehound found in the Weeping Quarry.
A presence bearing a title that associates it with an Old God, though the title names no particular one.

Karen No is a Bombadier in the infra-green bomber operation over the Bombardment. Kibli Killohertz's mission instructions direct pilots to request a bomber from her for sorties against Scourge forces.
The Infra-Green Flight Master is identified by that designation.
A Faceless Lurker prowls Icecrown as a hostile aberrant creature, using Seething Evil when it enters combat.
Skybreaker Infantry serve as the Alliance airship's soldiers in Icecrown. An infantryman can follow others, reflecting their role in an organized force.
A Frostbrood Spawn is a frostbrood creature that uses Frost Breath in combat.
Frostbrood Whelps are frostbrood creatures found in Icecrown. In combat, a whelp casts Corrosive Vial.
A Wyrm Reanimator is a Cult of the Damned caster at Sindragosa's Fall, where the cult raises frost wyrms from blue dragon bones. Reanimators fight with Corruption and Shadow Bolt.
Geargrinder's Jumpbot is a named mechanical construct encountered in Icecrown.

The Skybreaker Squad Leader is a field leader accompanying the Alliance assault on Ymirheim. His squad has suffered repeated ambushes from the vrykul, and he is determined to reach the gates and hold there for reinforcements. He rallies his troops with urgent calls to group up and watch for incoming attacks, and welcomes help in bringing the fight to the enemy. The escort operation is associated with Ground Commander Koup; the squad leader's immediate concern is his men's readiness and the assault.

A Cult of the Damned corrupter serving among the Scourge forces at Sindragosa's Fall. Koltira Deathweaver's assault targets these cultists as part of an effort to disrupt the raising of frost wyrms there. This corrupter is a hostile combatant, using bone armor in battle.
A defender of Ymirheim, serving the hostile vrykul forces in the area. This combatant attacks with a poisoned spear.
Necrotic Webspinners are hostile spiderlike creatures in the Ymirheim region. They attack with poison.
A Glacial Bonelord is an undead combatant in the Ymirheim region, striking with brutal blows and icy slashes.
Thunderbomb's Jumpbot is a mechanical construct associated with Thunderbomb.
A plague cauldron that can boil vigorously. Something can emerge from it, after which it continues to boil.
Thexal Deathchill is an undead figure encountered in Icecrown.

Frazzle Geargrinder is an Alliance engineer in Ymirheim, competing with Blast Thunderbomb in a jumpbot contest that puts engineering pride on the line. She is exuberant about the competition: after a successful run, she celebrates with a hug and calls the visitor her favorite hero.
A skeletal archmage encountered among others of its kind in Icecrown. It casts Frost Armor when drawn into combat.
An undead spiderlord, known as the Fallen Spiderlord.

Blast Thunderbomb is a goblin engineer representing the Warsong Offensive in a jumpbot contest against the Alliance. He boasts about his engineering and jumpbot, and worries that nearby frost vrykul will notice him. He frames the contest as a test of his engineering skill and Horde pride.

A Vrykul Necrolord is an undead vrykul combatant serving the Scourge forces at Sindragosa’s Fall. Koltira’s campaign targets necrolords there, and this necrolord casts Tug Soul, Shadow Bolt, and Shadow Nova in combat.
An oil slick.
Citadel Watcher is a humanoid watcher who attacks with Gargoyle Strike.

Ground Commander Koup directs troops in the assault on Ymirheim, where he has lost men to repeated vrykul ambushes. He asks for help getting his squad to the gates and protecting troop transports from automated spear guns, and regards the Ymirjar as especially dangerous. His replies show concern for his men and gratitude for help; he expects the operation to continue.
A decomposed ghoul serving as one of the Scourge targets in the Valley of Lost Hope. It is among the creatures a demolisher is sent to destroy and can enrage in combat.
A Frostskull magus among the Scourge targets in the Valley of Lost Hope. It is one of the creatures a demolisher is sent to destroy and uses Frostbolt in combat.
A bone giant among the Scourge targets in the Valley of Lost Hope. It is one of the creatures a demolisher is sent to destroy and uses Stomp in combat.
A Kor'kron infantryman deployed in the Ymirheim assault zone. This soldier can be directed to follow.

A Kor'kron squad leader whose unit is tasked with reaching Ymirheim's gates under fire and digging in for reinforcements. He rallies allies with calls to group up and watch for ambushes, and praises a capable fighter in the language of blood and honor.

Ground Commander Xutjja directs the Kor'kron ground assault near Ymirheim and coordinates efforts to get troops into the city by land and air. His orders are blunt and sometimes insulting, but his replies also show concern for the men facing a prolonged, costly attack and a need for reinforcements.
A blue dragon egg.

Rizzy Ratchwiggle is a named bombardier associated with the Scourge bombardment mission. Players are directed to speak with him for a bomber; his replies are terse and impatient, including a demand to be left alone while on duty.
A reanimated miner among the undead of Northrend, it attacks with puncturing and deep wounds.
A Scourge geist that scavenges demolisher parts from the Valley of Lost Hope.
A cruel overseer among the humanoid forces in the Ymirheim area.
A wrecked demolisher that can be restored to temporary working order with parts recovered from Scourge scavengers.

Ebon Blade markers in the Valley of Fallen Heroes mark places where a barricade kit can be used to construct defenses. Koltira directs the player to find them so barricades can help shield his forces as they move beyond Aldur'thar.

Darkspeaker R'khem is a chained creature in the Saronite Mines who communicates through painful, strange thoughts. He says the ymirjar captured him after he rose to investigate cavern noises, and asks for the foreman's key to free himself. His thoughts press against the listener, and he promises a reward before urging the listener to hand over the key.
Asric is a humanoid named in Northrend.
Jadaar is a humanoid named in Northrend.

Scourge Banner-Bearers are Scourge leaders who carry banners that empower the converted heroes they lead. Their banner aura marks their role in the Scourge’s effort to strengthen the dead in Icecrown.
A fallen hero's spirit is exhausted and haunted by a nightmare of fighting former friends. It wonders whether the nightmare has ended and asks for a moment's rest.
A Scourge war machine deployed in Icecrown's Valley of Lost Hope. It is a ground target for the Alliance bomber mission and explodes when destroyed.
A destroyed Scourge war machine, found among the wreckage in Icecrown.
A Scourge war engineer found among the war machines in Icecrown's Valley of Lost Hope.
A skeletal humanoid called the Skeletal Craftsman, found in the Icecrown region.
A Chosen Zealot found among the Scourge in Icecrown. It is a hulking combatant that uses Frailty.

A Skybreaker reconnaissance fighter, an autonomous flying craft encountered over Icecrown. Horde instructions identify these fighters as Alliance reconnaissance targets and direct the player to destroy them with an SGM-3.
An Orgrim’s Hammer scout posted in the Desolation area.
A Skybreaker troop transport involved in Alliance air drops at Ymirheim. Ground Commander Koup’s quest describes the troops’ drops and the effort to keep their transport alive.
A Cult of the Damned Dark Subjugator in the Desolation area. Its lines react to suddenly feeling strange and include an insistence that the speaker is a subjugator.
A Bitter Initiate is a Cult of the Damned caster whose combat routine includes Shadow Bolt and Corruption, making it one of the cult's hostile forces in Icecrown.

Highlord Tirion Fordring urges allies to keep their heads down, follow his lead and stand ready against the Lich King. He senses a dark presence and calls on the Light for strength and guidance. He challenges an opponent’s confidence by recalling how their last encounter ended.
The disguised crusader fights alongside Tirion's defenders. When Tirion falls, the crusader calls on the others to defend him with their lives, showing fierce resolve in protecting their leader.

This blue sample creature serves as a spell-hit target that grants kill credit. It is counted among the targets for sampling the cultists' cauldrons in Aldur'thar, a functional quest interaction rather than a speaking character.
Overseer Faedris is a Cult of the Damned overseer managing an encampment at Aldur’thar. In combat, he uses Arcane Blast and turns to Drain Life when badly wounded.
The Scourge raises dead heroes and turns them against the living as Converted Heroes. These undead combatants fight with Mortal Strike and an incapacitating shout.

A Scourge Converter is one of the Scourge forces operating in the Valley of Fallen Heroes and Icecrown Glacier west of Aldur'thar. The Scourge there raises the valley's dead and empowers converted heroes; this creature fights with frost magic.
A Cult of the Damned void summoner stationed in Aldur'thar, this caster attacks with Shadow Bolt.
A Cult of the Damned shadow channeler at Aldur'thar, this caster protects itself with Demon Armor when combat begins.
Overseer Veraj is a Cult of the Damned leader at Aldur'thar, one of the overseers managing an encampment in the gate operation. Veraj attacks with shadow and fire magic.
An animated laborer found in Aldur'thar, this creature fights with Puncture Wound.
A Cult of the Damned taskmaster in Icecrown. Its recorded combat action is Shadow Shock.
A wracked prisoner in Icecrown, held among the hostile forces there.
A Cult of the Damned blackguard in Icecrown. It uses Expose Armor and Sinister Strike, marking it as an armed close-combat guard.
A Harbinger of Horror serving among the Lich King's zealous defenders of Corp'rethar, the Horror Gate. It uses fear, chilling and frost attacks.
A Cult of the Damned torturer in Icecrown. It uses Shadow Word: Pain.
A Corp'rethar Guardian, one of the Lich King's zealous defenders of the Horror Gate in Icecrown. It uses Mortal Wound.
A Scourge Soulbinder that casts Frost Blast in combat.

Overseer Jhaeqon is a member of the Cult of the Damned and one of the overseers managing an operation at Aldur’thar. Thassarian and Koltira describe the overseers as leaders whose defeat would temporarily disrupt the Cult. Jhaeqon uses Shadowbolt in combat.
A Cult of the Damned apothecary found in the Aldur’thar area. Its combat orders include using a Fire Breath Potion.
A Cult of the Damned alchemist found in the Aldur’thar area. Its combat orders include throwing a Corrosive Vial.

Overseer Savryn is a member of the Cult of the Damned and one of the overseers managing an operation at Aldur’thar. Thassarian and Koltira describe the overseers as leaders whose defeat would temporarily disrupt the Cult. Savryn fights with Mutilate and Slice and Dice.
A Cult of the Damned researcher found in the Aldur’thar area. Its combat orders include Mind Blast and Wail of Souls.
A Bone Sentinel is an elite combatant that uses Mortal Strike in battle.
An Argent Mason is a member of the Argent cause whose role is masonry.
An Aldur'thar Sentry is a combat-ready sentry associated by name with Aldur'thar.
A Cult of the Damned Shard Watcher is a cultist spellcaster that attacks with Shadow Bolt Volley.
The Refurbished Demolisher is a rebuilt siege engine.

Matthias Lehner says he witnessed the prince create undead and argues that fighting the Scourge only swells its ranks. He describes the prince's greater power as killing former comrades, then offers to show how the army was made. His blunt dismissal of the player's understanding gives his lesson a grim, hard-edged tone.

Matthias Lehner warns that a demolisher can destroy hundreds or thousands of Scourge but cannot win the war. He directs its operator north to an old army encampment, promising a lesson about the enemy they face.
A Lordaeron captain who asks whether the visitor has come to address the men. His brief exchange suggests he helps marshal or organize the troops.

Matthias Lehner says only a visitor who touched something belonging to the king can see him. He knows that the Lich King is raising fallen blue dragons and asks the player to investigate by collecting whelp bone dust. He withholds what the visitor touched, fearing the king’s anger and warns that even mighty wyrms answered his call.

Fringe Engineer Tezzla drives the bombing effort, outfitting commandeered bombers with infra-green technology and urging pilots into missions against the Scourge. She praises successful gunners and sees promise in air offense, while briskly pressing for unmet quotas and calling for more bombing. When a mission succeeds, her greeting and praise are exuberant.
A plague cauldron target that begins to boil vigorously when the neutralizing dose is applied.

Kibli Killohertz directs bombing missions against the Scourge from the hidden bombardment position. The missions use infra-green shielding and bomber turrets and bomb launchers; Kibli jokes about lucky socks and in-laws, then teases returning pilots about their hand-eye coordination.
A powerful skeletal reaver found in Icecrown, this formidable undead combatant is vulnerable to the Dissolve spell.
An Ebon Blade initiate encountered in Icecrown.
An Ebon Blade geist encountered in Icecrown.
An Ebon Blade gargoyle encountered in Icecrown.
A powerful Bone Guard found in Icecrown, this skeletal combatant attacks with Mortal Strike.
Pustulent Colossus is an undead colossus encountered as a formidable foe. In combat, it uses a knockback attack.
Putridus the Ancient is a named giant. In combat, Putridus uses Putrid Punt and War Stomp.
An Ebon Blade vindicator is a humanoid member of the Ebon Blade.
A Scourge Deathcharger is an undead mount.
The Frostbrood Matriarch is an undead creature whose combat behavior includes a frost breath attack.
Hildana Deathstealer is a named undead combatant. She uses Lash and Touch of the Val'kyr during combat, with her attacks organized into changing combat phases.

Matthias Lehner recounts the prince’s near-fatal battle at the Court of Bones, asking the listener to find a bloodstained stone to understand what happened. He explains that after becoming king, the prince cast away his heart, which had remained a source of human feeling and weakness.
Glacier Penguins are critters found in several Northrend areas.
High Thane Jorfus is a named undead combatant found in Icecrown. He uses Blood Plague and Blood Strike in combat.
Ravaged Ghouls are undead creatures found in Icecrown. They use Festering Bite in combat.
A named presence of the Lich King.
A Vargul Wanderer is a hostile Vargul humanoid that casts Diminish Soul when it engages in combat.
A Cultist Acolyte is a cultist humanoid who casts Power Word: Fortitude on itself when attacked, can use Mind Flay, and heals itself when badly hurt.
Johnny Yes is a named elite humanoid encountered in Icecrown.
Willy Maybe is a named elite humanoid whose advice is to use a codename if captured.
An Alliance Infra-green Engineer is an engineer associated with the Alliance.
A Horde Infra-green Engineer.
Duchess Mynx is an Ebon Blade quartermaster in Icecrown. She offers goods to browse, serving as a local supplier for the order.
A Frostbrood Sentry is a hostile frostbrood guard in Icecrown. It can unleash Bitter Blast, fitting the role of a combat sentry.
A Gargoyle Ambusher is a hostile gargoyle encountered in Icecrown.
An enraged undead fleshrender classified as an elite creature.
A stitched undead brute in Icecrown.
A skeletal undead footsoldier in Icecrown.

Father Kamaros is a priest held amid the Scourge's work in Icecrown. He asks for help escaping so he can live to fight the Scourge again, and during his escape he urges the player to tell his brothers he is alive. He hopes to rejoin his comrades and praises those who aid him.

Sir Marcus Barlowe, the Master of Arms at the Argent Tournament Grounds, oversees a valiant's field training against Scourge-raised converted heroes. He reminds trainees that tournament practice should keep them ready for the continuing fight against the Scourge.

Captain Joseph Holley is Stormwind’s tournament horse master at the Argent Tournament Grounds. He urges Stormwind’s valiants to hone their skills in the grand melee and speaks with confidence in their ability to make the city proud. He also points toward the Argent Crusade’s campaign against the Scourge at Icecrown.

Marshal Jacob Alerius is Stormwind’s grand champion at the Argent Tournament, a proud representative of the city who welcomes champions into its tournament delegation. He guides aspiring valiants through training and challenges, and takes a personal interest in his arms: after a death knight broke his customary sword, he acquired Winter’s Edge and judged it superior enough to keep carrying. His words express loyalty to Stormwind and King Wrynn.
A melee training dummy used at the Argent Tournament Grounds, where aspiring champions can practice mounted combat.
A ranged training dummy at the Argent Tournament Grounds, set up for practicing ranged attacks.
Charge Target is a tournament training dummy in the Argent Tournament grounds.

The Sen'jin Valiant is a tournament combatant who invites challengers to fight. Its calls urge visitors to prepare, and its warning says a valiant bout is no simple task; after a win, it offers the opponent better luck next time.

The Orgrimmar Valiant is a tournament combatant who invites challengers to fight. Its calls urge visitors to prepare, and its warning says a valiant bout is no simple task; after a win, it offers the opponent better luck next time.

Corporal Arthur Flew serves as Stormwind Quartermaster at the Argent Tournament. He tells visitors that only Stormwind champions may purchase his goods, presenting the shop as a privilege reserved for champions.

Clara Tumblebrew, Mistress of Rams, represents Ironforge's tournament effort. She calls the grand melee important to Ironforge and urges competitors to train against other valiants, hoping they will make the city proud. She also frames the crusaders' fight at Icecrown as a test of their worth as allies.
Derrick Brindlebeard is Ironforge’s quartermaster at the Argent Tournament. He handles goods for Ironforge champions and makes clear that only they may purchase what he offers.

Lana Stouthammer is Ironforge’s Grand Champion at the Argent Tournament. She represents Ironforge in the grand melee and expects to make King Magni proud. After a death knight broke her customary sword, she chose Winter’s Edge, judging it superior and intending to carry it in the tournament.

Rollo Sureshot is Ironforge’s Master of Arms at the Argent Tournament. He treats competition as combat practice but insists the Scourge remains the real enemy, urging fighters to keep their edge against the Scourge and honor their allies.

Ambrose Boltspark, Grand Champion of Gnomeregan, welcomes valiants into the delegation and trains them for tournament competition. He values a finely balanced blade, and after hearing tales of Winter's Edge, chooses it over repairing his customary sword.

Mokra the Skullcrusher, Grand Champion of Orgrimmar, welcomes proven fighters to its delegation and expects them to train with his men. Blunt about the competition, he boasts that Orgrimmar's champions will prevail. After a death knight breaks his customary sword, he seeks Winter's Edge and decides to keep it rather than finish repairs.

Zul'tore is the Darkspear troll Grand Champion of Sen'jin, leading the city's tournament delegation and overseeing valiant training and tests before the grand melee. He urges valiants to learn rival cities' fighting styles and earn seals, framing their advancement as bringing glory to the Darkspear. He worries that Alliance champions seeking ancient blades could gain an advantage; when his tournament blade goes missing before a match, he sends a champion to recover a replacement.

Deathstalker Visceri is the Forsaken Grand Champion of the Undercity and leads its tournament delegation. He invites recruits to train as valiants, testing themselves against other cities' fighters and preparing for higher competition. After a death knight breaks his tournament sword, Visceri seeks Winter's Edge; once it is recovered, he says he will carry it instead of finishing repairs on his customary blade.

Eressea Dawnsinger is Silvermoon's Grand Champion and a proud mentor to its valiants, welcoming proven combatants into the delegation and encouraging them to test themselves against rival cities. After a death knight broke her customary sword, she took up Winter's Edge and says she will keep carrying it.
A Silvermoon valiant in the Argent Tournament's city contests, this fighter challenges opponents to a demanding match and urges them to prepare. Their brief boasts keep attention on the contest.
A Thunder Bluff valiant in the Argent Tournament's city contests, this fighter challenges opponents to a demanding match and urges them to prepare. Their brief boasts keep attention on the contest.

An Undercity valiant calls challengers to ready themselves and warns that fighting a valiant is no simple task. In the arena's exchange, the valiant also says, “I have won. Better luck another time, friend.”

Runok Wildmane is the Grand Champion of Thunder Bluff's delegation, welcoming recruits beneath its banner and urging them to fight honorably and bravely. He is also personally invested in his arms: after a death knight breaks his customary sword, he seeks Winter's Edge and says he will continue to carry that superior blade.

Akinos, the Argent Tournament's Master of Arms, treats the contest as preparation for the greater fight against the Scourge. He urges trainees to keep their combat skills sharp while competing, and directs them against Scourge-raised converted heroes to honor the tournament's allies.

Crusader Rhydalla investigates the murders surrounding the tournament’s Black Knight, seeking evidence that connects him to the killings. She uses a seer’s crystal imbued with the Light to expose deception, and treats recovered orders as evidence of his Cult of the Damned allegiance. The threat to the champions troubles her, as does the possibility that the Argent Crusade has been manipulated.

An elite undead lieutenant in the Boneguard forces of the Lich King at the Court of Bones. Argent Crusade riders target lieutenants during their mounted assault preparations against the forces at Icecrown Citadel. It casts Defend.
Goblin Bezzle Blastbolt speaks for the Blastbolt brothers, boasting that no one builds faster, cheaper, or better than they do.
Bozzle Blastbolt is a humanoid in Northrend.

Boneguard Footmen are common foot soldiers among the Lich King's minions around Corp'rethar in the Court of Bones. Argent Crusade forces target them while preparing to assault Icecrown Citadel; one account describes their masses as vulnerable to mounted crusaders.

Squire David is a human child at the Aspirants' Ring. He asks whether challengers are ready to fight a valiant of the Argent Crusade and says he will call forth a member when they are ready to test for that rank. The gossip also offers an explanation of how Argent Crusade riders fight.

The Orgrimmar Champion resents the tournament's mounted-combat rules. He longs to fight with his axe, and objects to using a long pole and urging his wolf to charge without attacking. He sees the Alliance as enemies in a war declared by their king, and feels the contest keeps him from fighting as his people should.
An Orgrimmar valiant of the Argent Tournament.

The Gnomeregan Champion doubts his chances against larger competitors and calculates that his odds of success are distressingly low. He is anxious about managing the mathematics of his turbostrider's charge while keeping his lance and shield precisely positioned.
A Gnomeregan valiant of the Argent Tournament.

The Undercity Champion meets the tournament’s fighting with irreverent humor: he claims to have punched a penguin, then admits he only wanted to see the listener’s reaction. His laughter reinforces the joke.

The Silvermoon Champion sounds weary of the endless fighting and dismisses the tournament’s posturing and ring dances as pointless. Even so, his complaints turn briefly to the indignity of helmet hair.
A Silvermoon Valiant, identified with Silvermoon and present in the tournament area. The supplied evidence gives no personal speech or further individual history.
An Undercity Valiant, identified with Undercity and present in the tournament area. The supplied evidence gives no personal speech or further individual history.
A Thunder Bluff Valiant, identified with Thunder Bluff and present in the tournament area. The supplied evidence gives no personal speech or further individual history.
A Sen'jin Champion, identified with Sen'jin and present in the tournament area. The supplied evidence gives no personal speech or further individual history.
A Sen'jin Valiant, identified with Sen'jin and present in the tournament area. The supplied evidence gives no personal speech or further individual history.

The Stormwind Champion feels the weight of his duty as people die without his protection, and says his orders keep him at the tournament despite finding the fighting empty. His words to a Confessor suggest he is troubled by this conflict.
A Stormwind-affiliated valiant stationed at the tournament grounds.
An Ironforge champion with an awkward confession: while listening to a sermon, he felt powerful urges that are now driving him nuts.
An Ironforge-affiliated valiant stationed at the tournament grounds.
The Black Knight's gryphon is a gryphon associated with him, serving as an animal companion or mount.
Squire Danny serves at the Argent Tournament's mounted challenges. When a competitor selects the ready-to-fight option, he summons an Argent Champion as their opponent.

Squire Cavin serves at the Argent Tournament's champions' practice ring, where he is tasked with summoning knights for practice bouts. He also has a role in calling the Black Knight to face a champion's challenge.
A humanoid conspirator of the Cult of the Damned encountered in Icecrown.

Kethiel Sunlance is a Master of Arms at the Argent Tournament, associated with field training that keeps valiants prepared to fight the Scourge. His training assignment frames tournament practice as preparation for the wider threat.

Dern Ragetotem is a Master of Arms at the Argent Tournament, associated with field training that keeps valiants prepared to fight the Scourge. His training assignment frames tournament practice as preparation for the wider threat.

At the Argent Tournament Grounds, Shadow Hunter Mezil-kree is the Master of Arms. His field-training brief treats practice against fellow competitors and readiness for the Scourge as parts of the same work; after training, he gives a quiet nod to keeping one’s edge.

At the Argent Tournament Grounds, Sarah Chalke is the Mistress of Arms. Her field-training brief treats practice against fellow competitors and readiness for the Scourge as parts of the same work; after training, she gives a quiet nod to keeping one’s edge.

Magister Edien Sunhollow represents the Sunreavers at the Argent Tournament, registering and training aspirants while helping champions seek Northrend blades drawn from old tales. He tests those stories against the weapons’ quality, and his congratulations and practical arrangements keep competitors moving through their training.
Sunreaver Guardians stand watch at the Argent Tournament Grounds, a visible guard presence for the Sunreavers.

Morah Worgsister, the Mistress of Wolves, trains Horde valiants for the Argent Tournament’s mounted grand melee. She is confident her warriors will win and urges practice until rider and wolf move as one. She also sends trained riders against the Lich King’s forces near Icecrown Citadel, praising their bravery.

Gahju, the Master of Raptors, trains Horde valiants for the Argent Tournament’s mounted grand melee. He says practice against other valiants will prepare them to win, and encourages them to keep at it. He also sends trained riders against the Lich King’s forces near Icecrown Citadel, praising their fearlessness.
The Black Knight is a humanoid.

Handler Dretch is the horse master at the Argent Tournament Grounds. He prepares challengers for the grand melee with a stabled Forsaken warhorse, stressing that rider and mount must work as one. He calls the melee the tournament’s most important contest and voices confidence in victory. He also directs mounted attacks on Boneguard forces at Court of Bones as part of the Argent Crusade’s preparations against Icecrown Citadel.

Aneera Thuron is the hawkstrider mistress at the Argent Tournament Grounds. She prepares challengers for the grand melee with a stabled Silvermoon hawkstrider, stressing that rider and mount must work as one. She calls the melee the tournament’s most important contest and voices confidence in victory. She also directs mounted attacks on Boneguard forces at Court of Bones as part of the Argent Crusade’s preparations against Icecrown Citadel.

Anka Clawhoof is the kodo mistress at the Argent Tournament Grounds. She prepares challengers for the grand melee with a stabled Mulgore kodo, stressing that rider and mount must work as one. She calls the melee the tournament’s most important contest and voices confidence in victory. She also directs mounted attacks on Boneguard forces at Court of Bones as part of the Argent Crusade’s preparations against Icecrown Citadel.
A Boneguard Scout serves among the Lich King's minions in the Court of Bones, where Argent Crusaders target scouts as part of their push toward Icecrown Citadel. It is a battlefield creature.

Freka Bloodaxe is Orgrimmar's quartermaster at the Argent Tournament Grounds. In her terse greeting, she makes clear that her goods are intended for Orgrimmar champions, giving her a direct, guarded manner.

Samamba represents Sen'jin as a quartermaster at the Argent Tournament Grounds. Her greeting, delivered in a distinctive Troll dialect, briskly corrects visitors who approach the wrong quartermaster and frames her goods as intended for Sen'jin champions.

Eliza Killian is Undercity's quartermaster at the Argent Tournament Grounds. Her greeting opens with a sharp dismissal before stating that her goods are for Undercity champions, giving her a notably brusque public manner.

Doru Thunderhorn serves as Thunder Bluff's quartermaster at the Argent Tournament Grounds. His greeting begins with an apology before explaining that his goods are intended for Thunder Bluff champions, giving his manner a courteous and measured tone.

Trellis Morningsun is Silvermoon's quartermaster at the Argent Tournament Grounds. Her greeting uses formal, ceremonious language as she explains that her goods are intended for Silvermoon champions, setting her apart with a polished public manner.

A Gnomeregan Valiant in the Argent Tournament, this level-80 combatant challenges others to prove themselves in a joust. The valiant warns that the contest is no simple task and, after victory, offers a friendly wish of better luck next time.

A Darnassus Valiant in the Argent Tournament, this level-80 combatant challenges others to prove themselves in a joust. The valiant warns that the contest is no simple task and, after victory, offers a friendly wish of better luck next time.
An Exodar Champion, a humanoid.

A Stormwind Valiant in the Argent Tournament, this level-80 combatant challenges others to prove themselves in a joust. The valiant warns that the contest is no simple task and, after victory, offers a friendly wish of better luck next time.

An Exodar Valiant in the Argent Tournament, this level-80 combatant challenges others to prove themselves in a joust. The valiant warns that the contest is no simple task and, after victory, offers a friendly wish of better luck next time.

An Ironforge Valiant ready to meet challengers. Before a fight, they caution that a valiant is no simple opponent, then call for their rival to prepare. After winning, they acknowledge the contest and wish their opponent better luck next time.
A Darnassus Valiant in Icecrown. The city and valiant title identify this combatant.
An Exodar Valiant in Icecrown. The city and valiant title identify this combatant.
Dustin Vail is a Grand Master Tailoring Trainer at the tournament grounds in Icecrown. His named role marks him as a specialist in the region's tailoring trade.
Kul'de is a Grand Master Leatherworking Trainer recorded at the tournament grounds in Icecrown. The name and title identify a specialist in the region's leatherworking trade.
Fael Morningsong is a Grand Master Enchanting Trainer recorded at the tournament grounds in Icecrown. The name and title identify a specialist in the region's enchanting trade.
Binkie Brightgear is the Grand Master Engineering Trainer stationed in Northrend.
Bethany Cromwell is the Grand Master Cooking Trainer stationed in Northrend.
Crystal Brightspark is the Grand Master Alchemy Trainer stationed in Northrend.
Joseph Wilson is the Grand Master First Aid Trainer stationed in Northrend. He follows a route, pausing and turning to face a set direction while making his rounds.
Oluros is the Grand Master Jewelcrafting Trainer stationed in Northrend.
Rekka the Hammer is the Grand Master Blacksmithing Trainer stationed in Northrend.

Jaelyne Evensong is Darnassus’s Grand Champion at the Argent Tournament. She welcomes recruits to train and compete beside her delegation, encouraging valiants to learn other cities’ fighting styles before facing an Argent champion. She seeks enchanted blades to overcome a disadvantage and regards Winter’s Edge as superior to her customary weapon.

Colosos is the Exodar’s Grand Champion at the Argent Tournament. He welcomes a recruit to the delegation and presents valiant training as preparation for city contests and a test against an Argent champion. He values shared training and competition for honor and renown, and speaks of fighting the Scourge alongside the Argent Crusade.
Fizzix Blastbolt is an engineering supplies merchant in Northrend.
Mera Mistrunner is a cooking supplies merchant in Northrend.

Meline Duskpath is a tailoring supplies merchant in Northrend. Her listed role is focused on tailoring goods, distinguishing her from the nearby specialists in cooking, engineering, enchanting, inscription, and jewelcrafting supplies.

Liere Morningsong is an enchanting supplies merchant in Northrend. Her listed role is focused on enchanting goods, distinguishing her from the nearby specialists in cooking, engineering, tailoring, inscription, and jewelcrafting supplies.
Fanii is an inscription supplies merchant in Northrend.
Anuur is a jewelcrafting supplies merchant in Northrend.

Arcanist Taelis represents the Silver Covenant at the Argent Tournament, welcoming recruits and guiding aspirants through mounted training and their challenge. He also helps the Covenant’s champions seek ancient Northrend weapons, drawing on local legends and reports; once an aspirant proves ready, he directs them to their city delegation.
One of the Silver Covenant guardians stationed at the Argent Tournament pavilion, among a group of twelve assigned there.
Ellia Moondancer sells fresh food at the Argent Tournament grounds.
Jenna Thunderbrew sells refreshments at the Argent Tournament grounds.

Avareth Swiftstrike, of the Silver Covenant, guides aspirants at the Argent Tournament Grounds through mounted combat and preparation against the Scourge. He reminds them that the Scourge remains the real enemy even as they test their skills against peers, and frames the challenge as one to meet with honor and bravery.

Scout Shalyndria, of the Silver Covenant, trains aspirants in mounted combat at the Argent Tournament Grounds. She recognizes that mounted fighting can be difficult for warriors used to fighting on foot, and stresses practice and learning to break an opponent's defenses as essential to success in the tournament.

Tickin Gearspanner is the Argent Tournament's Master of Arms. He sends valiant aspirants to fight Scourge-raised heroes, presenting field exercises as a way to stay sharp against the enemy while honing skills against competitors. When they return, he expresses confidence that they will make his side proud when competition begins.

Flickin Gearspanner, Master of Mechanostriders at the Argent Tournament, urges competitors to prepare for the Grand Melee by testing themselves against valiants from other Alliance capitals. Flickin expects them to make their delegation proud and sends them to fight the Lich King’s minions alongside crusaders in the Court of Bones.
Rillie Spindlenut serves as Gnomeregan Quartermaster. Rillie greets visitors courteously and apologizes when explaining that only champions of Gnomeregan may buy the goods on offer.

Illestria Bladesinger, Mistress of Arms at the Argent Tournament, values competition as practice but warns that the Scourge remains the real enemy. She urges combat against Scourge-raised heroes both to honor allies and to maintain readiness for battle.
Rook Hawkfist serves as Darnassus Quartermaster, expressing regret when explaining that only champions of Darnassus may purchase the goods on offer.

Airae Starseeker is the Mistress of Nightsabers at the Argent Tournament grounds. Her grand melee training is framed around Darnassus's hope to win and practice against rival Alliance valiants. She also speaks of cooperation with the Argent Crusade in the fight against the Lich King's forces.

Saandos is the Master of Arms at the Argent Tournament grounds. He treats tournament practice as only part of staying ready: his field training sends competitors against Scourge-raised fallen heroes, and he welcomes them back from those exercises with a reminder that the Scourge remains a threat.

Ranii is the Mistress of Elekks at the Argent Tournament grounds. Her grand melee training centers on the Exodar's hope to win and practice against rival Alliance valiants, with competitors taking to the ring on Azuremyst elekks. She also presents Exodar warriors as more than parade-ground decoration when praising their service against the Scourge.

Irisee serves as the Exodar Quartermaster at the Argent Tournament grounds. Her wares are reserved for champions of the Exodar, tying her work specifically to Exodar competitors and their standing in the tournament.

Amariel Sunsworn is a Sunreaver at the Argent Tournament who insists that aspirants keep their hard-won combat skills ready against the Scourge, and earn the right to compete through honorable, brave service. For mounted-charge training, she sends riders to Rugan Steelbelly to learn the attack.
