Galathia Brightdawn is a Sunreaver mounted-combat instructor at the Argent Tournament. She has riders practice lance abilities against training dummies and stresses that breaking an opponent's defenses can decide a match. Patient with newcomers to mounted combat, she has a dry edge when comparing their progress with that of some warriors.

Chillmaw is a frost wyrm leading a Cult of the Damned raiding party near the Argent Tournament. A formidable airborne threat, Chillmaw uses frost breath in combat and is associated with cultist bombardiers.
An Argent Peacekeeper, a humanoid.
A Darnassus Champion and one of the Argent Tournament's city champions. In combat, the champion calls for challengers to ready themselves and wishes them better luck after winning.
An Exodar Champion and one of the Argent Tournament's city champions. In combat, the champion calls for challengers to ready themselves and wishes them better luck after winning.
A Gnomeregan Champion and one of the Argent Tournament's city champions. In combat, the champion calls for challengers to ready themselves and wishes them better luck after winning.
An Ironforge Champion and one of the Argent Tournament's city champions. In combat, the champion calls for challengers to ready themselves and wishes them better luck after winning.

The Orgrimmar Champion is one of the champions who can be challenged in the Argent Tournament. The tournament’s warning describes a champion fight as no simple task; this opponent calls challengers to ready themselves and, after winning, offers them better luck next time.

The Sen'jin Champion is one of the champions who can be challenged in the Argent Tournament. The tournament’s warning describes a champion fight as no simple task; this opponent calls challengers to ready themselves and, after winning, offers them better luck next time.

The Silvermoon Champion is one of the champions who can be challenged in the Argent Tournament. The tournament’s warning describes a champion fight as no simple task; this opponent calls challengers to ready themselves and, after winning, offers them better luck next time.

The Stormwind Champion is one of the champions who can be challenged in the Argent Tournament. The tournament’s warning describes a champion fight as no simple task; this opponent calls challengers to ready themselves and, after winning, offers them better luck next time.

A Thunder Bluff champion at the Argent Tournament, this combatant calls opponents to ready themselves and warns that facing a champion is no simple task. The challenge is framed as a personal fight; after claiming victory, the champion wishes the opponent better luck next time.

An Undercity champion at the Argent Tournament, this combatant calls opponents to ready themselves and warns that facing a champion is no simple task. The challenge is framed as a personal fight; after claiming victory, the champion wishes the opponent better luck next time.

npcs.name: Eadric the Pure

records.text: Eadric the Pure is the Grand Champion of the Argent Crusade at the Argent Tournament. At the highlord's request, he helps coordinate champions' training and the tournament grounds' defenses. He speaks of the honor of representing the Crusade and asks whether allies have fought the enemy in Icecrown.

npcs.title: Grand Champion of the Argent Crusade

npcs.name: Crok Scourgebane

records.text: Crok Scourgebane is a Grand Champion of the Ebon Blade at the Argent Tournament. He distrusts the Argent Crusade's protection, faulting its peacekeepers and skytalons for breaking up brawls while the Scourge threatens the grounds, and insists that his own protect their allies. His campaign against the Scourge is defiant and martial.

npcs.title: Grand Champion of the Ebon Blade

records.text: Cellian Daybreak is the Argent Tournament's Master of Arms. He urges champions to carry their arena prowess into the struggle against the Scourge, and presents vigilance as a duty shared by his brethren and each champion's own people. His encouragement focuses on taking tournament skill into the wider war.

At the Argent Tournament Grounds, Zor'be the Bloodletter serves as a Master of Arms and urges combatants to take the Scourge seriously amid tournament preparations. He frames fighting the Cult of the Damned as proof of the Horde's commitment to the Argent Crusade's war, then asks whether you have tested yourself against the Scourge.

Illyrie Nightfall, Mistress of Horses at the Argent Tournament Grounds, sends champions to practice mounted lance combat against representatives of the cities in the Ring of Champions. She stresses continued training and learning opponents' weaknesses, and praises a rider's handling of their mount while warning that competitors will learn to fear them.

Luuri, Mistress of Horses at the Argent Tournament Grounds, recommends practice against the champions in the Ring, warning that defeated rivals may return seeking revenge. Her training advice focuses on mounted lance combat and learning from opponents; in her completion remarks, she praises the practice as preparation and voices support for either Alliance or Horde champions, according to the quest version.
A hippogryph associated with the Argent Tournament, found on the tournament grounds.

Fhyron Shadesong, of the Cenarion Circle, tends young growth on a wind-cut bluff in Icecrown, where he says most life has fled. He coaxes trees to grow and hopes they will one day tower over the bluff; his remarks to a small plant are patient and encouraging.
A stabled elekk associated with Exodar, present at the Argent Tournament grounds.
A stabled hawkstrider associated with Silvermoon, present at the Argent Tournament grounds.
A stabled kodo associated with Thunder Bluff, present at the Argent Tournament grounds.
A Gnomeregan mechanostrider kept among the stabled mounts.
A Darnassian nightsaber kept among the stabled mounts.
An Ironforge ram kept among the stabled mounts.
A Darkspear raptor kept among the stabled mounts.
A Forsaken warhorse kept among the stabled mounts. It is an undead creature.
An Orgrimmar wolf kept among the stabled mounts.
A Stormwind steed kept among the stabled mounts.

Justicar Mariel Trueheart is the Argent Crusade's seneschal at the Argent Tournament and welcomes visitors on its behalf. She says the Crusade wants champions from every city to train together against their mutual Scourge enemy, and directs new entrants to their faction's representative. She identifies Eadric the Pure as the brotherhood's grand champion, overseeing champion training and final preparations for competition.
A Sunreaver hawkstrider kept among the mounts at the Argent Tournament stables.
A Quel'dorei steed kept among the mounts at the Argent Tournament stables.
Helidan Lightwing serves as a flight master at the Argent Tournament. Travelers can ask him for fast travel; when attacked, he summons an enraged gryphon or wyvern.

Broxel Goldgrasp is an enthusiastic tournament souvenir seller, urging visitors to take home gifts for their families and wear city or champion colors. He offers doublets as an alternative to tabards and encourages supporters to show their allegiance at the bouts.
Thomas Partridge is a stablemaster who handles pet stabling and lost companion recovery. His duties include following a regular route through the area.
Makuli is a fresh food vendor serving visitors at the tournament grounds.
Akrittok is a fresh food vendor serving visitors at the tournament grounds.
Tingiyok is a refreshments vendor serving visitors at the tournament grounds.
Torngasak is a refreshments vendor serving visitors at the tournament grounds.
A stabled Argent warhorse at the tournament grounds, this animal is a horse.
Julie Osworth is the reagent seller identified by her Reagents title. Her vendor role centers on reagents, and the local shop menu lets visitors browse her goods.
Torgah is a general-goods seller whose title identifies his shop, with ammunition among his vendor services. The local shop menu lets visitors browse his goods.
Caris Sunlance is an innkeeper. Caris welcomes weary travelers, and the inn menu includes an option to make the inn a home, linking this named host to the grounds' hospitality.
Jarin Dawnglow is an innkeeper. Jarin welcomes weary travelers, and the inn menu includes an option to make the inn a home, linking this named host to the grounds' hospitality.

Rugan Steelbelly teaches mounted charge combat at the Argent Tournament Grounds. He stresses that a rider needs a tournament mount and lance, then demonstrates breaking a target's shield before charging while it is vulnerable. His role is practical instruction in the tournament's mounted fighting.

Jeran Lockwood is the Argent Tournament’s Master of the Melee, stationed at the training area north of the grounds and east of the Aspirants’ Ring. He trains Aspirants in mounted close combat, teaching them to defend themselves while thrusting at melee targets.

Valis Windchaser is the Argent Tournament’s Master of the Shield-Breaker, stationed at the training area north of the grounds and east of the Aspirants’ Ring. He teaches mounted combatants to use the Shield-Breaker against ranged targets, including how to exploit a target left vulnerable by the attack.

Argent Confessor Paletress welcomes visitors to her chapel of the Light and offers a respite from the world’s troubles. She speaks of the Scourge threat and counsels champions that serving the Light means more than small strikes against its vast undead host. Her guidance is encouraging but firm, and she urges them to fight well.
A campaign warhorse kept in the stables, ready for a rider.

Boneguard Commanders are Lich King forces in the Court of Bones, where crusaders prepare an assault on Icecrown Citadel. The campaign calls for mounted crusaders to destroy these commanders, and they use the Defend ability.
An Argent Peacekeeper, a humanoid member of the Argent forces.
Crusader Maran is a specifically named crusader among the humanoid Argent forces.

Squire Artie is a cheerful, informal squire who helps raise money for the Argent Crusade. He invites visitors to contribute and thanks them, saying he knows the crusade will put the money to good use. He also points visitors toward Confessor Paletress’s sermon, where seating can be hard to find.

A captive aspirant held by the Cult of the Damned at Deathspeaker's Watch, this tournament hopeful is frightened and urgently concerned for the other prisoners. One pleads for help as the captives are killed; another regrets coming to the tournament. The aspirants were captured after following Crusader Kul the Reckless in an assault on the cultists.

A Cult of the Damned zealot stationed at Deathspeaker's Watch, serving among the cultists who captured the aspirants and Crusader Kul the Reckless. This is a hostile cult member, identified by the Cult of the Damned affiliation.

A Cult of the Damned ritualist stationed at Deathspeaker's Watch, participating in the cult's hostile presence there. In combat, the ritualist casts Mind Sear, reflecting a battle role alongside its ritual function.

Girana the Blooded is a Sunreaver at the Argent Tournament Grounds who helps oppose the Kvaldir. She backs the Sunreavers as allies of the Argent Crusade, mocks Kul for getting himself and aspirants into trouble again, and relishes needling the Silver Covenant. Though she says Sunreavers and crusaders do not always agree, she credits Confessor Paletress with teaching her much.
Vasarin Redmorn is the Sunreavers' quartermaster at the Argent Tournament Grounds, where he offers goods for browsing.
Gormok Zealot is a humanoid encountered in Dragonblight.
Immuyak tends Gormok's creatures and has reservations about their slaughter, accepting it at least so Gormok can have his chance to fight.
Argent Crusade accounts describe Deathspeaker Kharos as a ruthless Cult of the Damned commander at Deathspeaker's Watch, overseeing fortifications for an attack on the tournament grounds.

Narasi Snowdawn is a Silver Covenant representative at the Argent Tournament grounds. She urges action against Kvaldir raiders who threaten supplies and tuskarr villagers at Hrothgar's Landing. After hearing Confessor Paletress, Narasi says the Covenant must take up the crusaders' mission, and she is grateful when the slain villagers receive last rites.
As Silver Covenant quartermaster at the Argent Tournament grounds, Hiren Loresong handles the faction's goods; visitors can open his vendor list by choosing to browse.

High Crusader Adelard serves at the Argent Tournament Grounds, where he tasks champions with quests for the Crusade and tournament. He sees a crusader’s role as more than fighting evil: champions should exemplify the cause and rally their people. His response to a victory over Drottinn Hrothgar describes it as buying the Crusade time.

Dame Evniki Kapsalis is the Argent Crusade’s Crusader’s Quartermaster at the tournament grounds. Tirion has charged her with finding heroes exalted among the Crusade and its allied peoples, then awarding them appropriate decorations. Her dialogue describes these rewards as reserved for those who have earned the title of Crusader.

Savinia Loresong is a Silver Covenant member helping the Argent Crusade with tournament beast care. She resents being assigned Gormok, saying the creature and the Sunreavers are alike and that she would rather the Sunreavers handle it. She says her faction will honor its agreement to do what the Crusade asks, while criticizing the Sunreavers for not showing the same cooperation.

Tylos Dawnrunner is a Sunreaver helping the Argent Crusade with tournament beast care. He complains about handling Gormok and says the Silver Covenant should have been given the task, then predicts they will be fragile and fussy allies in the battle for Icecrown Citadel. He says the Sunreavers will honor their agreement to do what the Crusade asks, while criticizing the Silver Covenant for not doing likewise.

Kul the Reckless is a crusader who led aspirants against the cultists at Deathspeaker’s Watch without reinforcements and was captured with them. Those seeking his rescue describe this as another of his troublesome exploits. Kul says his captors were about to strap him to an altar and drain his soul, and urgently wants to escape.

Crusader Silverdawn seeks peace for fallen heroes whose spirits the Scourge turn against their comrades. As the campaign progresses, Silverdawn worries about suffering the same fate and hopes someone would grant that rest rather than force fellow crusaders to kill them repeatedly. Silverdawn also seeks to save sailors trapped by the Kvaldir and their kraken, and criticizes the Silver Covenant and Sunreavers for charging ahead without listening.
A Sacrificed Aspirant, a humanoid.
A Black Knight Caster.
Doctor Kohler is described as an infamous doctor whom Crusader Rhydalla suspects of practicing among the cultists near the tournament grounds. Rhydalla seeks evidence of his plans.
A stabled Argent hippogryph appears anxious and ready to go. Its conversation offers a mount-up option to prepare for battle, which triggers Mount Up when selected.
Steen Horngrass is a stable master. He offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Moonbell is a stable master. She offers help recovering lost companions and access to pet stabling.
Froggle is identified as Steen Horngrass's pet at the Argent Tournament Grounds.
Anmarie is Moonbell's named pet.
A sailor identified with the Crimson Dawn, encountered in Northrend.
A sailor identified with the Silver Blade, encountered in Northrend.
A North Sea shark, an animal of the waters around Northrend.
Bognar Ironfoot is a stable master who handles pet stabling and lost-companion recovery. His greeting offers assistance with these services.
Gormok the Impaler is a named humanoid combatant, distinguished by his personal epithet.
Icehowl is a beast.
Huntsman Yahto describes a fierce, cunning yeti as one of the strongest of its kind. He says they keep it asleep with herbs in its food, but warns that it will not be lethargic in the ring.
An Argent Tournament post.
The visiting warlocks are warlocks who say their powers are respected on the battlefront, where they work beyond the bounds of polite society.

Wilfred Fizzlebang is a summoner invited to the tournament to summon a demon for its competitors. He loudly calls himself a master summoner, insists demons fear his will, and expects the world to know and fear his name once his summoning is complete.
A hungry jormungar beast.

In a remark about Gormok, Huntsman Hakan says keeping the magnataur until his time is difficult, though he is bound tightly enough to pose no danger. He also cautions that magnataur are not as foolish as they seem.
Huntsman Lokni says his group has tended the worms for some time and hopes they will be ready for the ring event, where challengers face two jormungar.

Herald Beluus is the Voice of the Argent Tournament, a public announcer whose calls announce the arrivals of Horde leaders, Tirion Fordring, Varian Wrynn and Jaina Proudmoore, and direct the crowd to make way.
Arcanist Asarina is an Emblem of Triumph Quartermaster whose goods are available to browse.
Magistrix Iruvia is the Emblem of Triumph quartermaster in the Argent Tournament grounds, where visitors can browse her goods.
Champion Isimode is a triumphant armor vendor in the Argent Tournament grounds, offering goods to visitors.
Champion Faesrol is a triumphant armor vendor in the Argent Tournament grounds, offering goods to visitors.
Valiant Laradia is a triumphant armor vendor in the Argent Tournament grounds. Her recorded level is 79.
Valiant Bressia is a triumphant armor vendor in the Argent Tournament grounds. Her recorded level is 79.
Aspirant Forudir is a triumphant armor vendor in the Argent Tournament grounds. His recorded level is 78.
Aspirant Naradiel is a vendor of Triumphant armor who offers visitors the chance to browse the goods.
Swift Alliance Steed is a riding steed associated with the Alliance.
Sunreaver Dragonhawk is a dragonhawk associated with the Sunreavers.
Fjola Lightbane is a named undead figure.
Eydis Darkbane is a named undead figure.
A humanoid named Argent Custodian.
Priestess Alorah is a humanoid who casts Cosmetic Chains out of combat.
Priest Grimmin is a humanoid who casts Cosmetic Chains out of combat.
Anthar Forgemender is a humanoid.
Baelnor Lightbearer is a humanoid.
Noozle Whizzlestick is a humanoid.
Melador Valestrider is an elemental creature.
A humanoid named Shocuul.
Caiphus the Stern is a humanoid.
A humanoid named Malithus Brightblade.
A humanoid named Maz'dinah.
A humanoid named Narrhok Steelbreaker.
A humanoid named Harkzog.
A tiny scarab found across several parts of Icecrown.
A swift wolf associated with the Horde and found in Icecrown. It is a beast, known here by its speed and its connection to the Horde.

Caladis Brightspear is a Silver Covenant questgiver devoted to restoring Quel'Delar. He recognizes the blade as dragonforged and vows that the Covenant will see it restored. A recovered hilt seems familiar to him, and he recognizes the blade's symbols, but its precise identity and how it reached Icecrown remain a mystery to him. He believes dragons forged it and gifted it to a mortal people.

Myralion Sunblaze is a Sunreaver involved in restoring Quel'Delar. He studies its style and markings as possible signs of dragonforging and insists the Sunreavers must see it restored. Seeing the blade of Thalorien Dawnseeker fills him with wonder and pride for the sin'dorei; when evidence shows that even a great dragonforged creation can be corrupted, he urges the bearer to heed Uther's advice quickly.
A Silver Covenant sentinel stationed among the faction's forces in the area. It warns a visitor it takes for a minion of the Lich King that they are not welcome.
A Sunreaver war mage serving among the faction's spellcasters in the area.

Drugan Deepdraught is an Explorer's League representative interested in the mystery of Quel'Delar. He considers the sword far older than dwarven work and says he is preparing a report for Brann, while noting that Sunreaver and Silver Covenant representatives are also investigating it.
An Argent commander representing the Argent presence across several regions.
An Ebon Blade commander representing the Ebon Blade presence across several regions.
An Argent hippogryph.
An Argent Crusader serving among the Argent Crusade's ranks.
A Knight of the Ebon Blade.

place_records.text: You are in Icecrown, a land in Northrend that neither the Alliance nor the Horde holds. Death's Rise, the Shadow Vault, the Argent Vanguard, Ymirheim and Crusaders' Pinnacle are its main settlements, and none belongs to a side. Scourge undead and vrykul are the main dangers, and Forgotten Depths nerubians pour through the breach at the Argent Vanguard.

You are in Onslaught Harbor, where Scarlet Onslaught ships rest in the harbor below Death's Rise. Gryphon riders, guards, paladins and darkweavers of the Scarlet Onslaught make it dangerous, and the ravenous jaws of sharks in the water threaten anyone nearby.

You are in Death's Rise, a death knight base in Icecrown with a flight master, repairs and a vendor. Lord-Commander Arete commands the death knights here and pursues the Scarlet Onslaught in the harbor below, while Setaal Darkmender and Uzo Deathcaller work on captured Onslaught gryphons and the dead. Dead vrykul walk the grounds.

You are in The Shadow Vault, an Ebon Blade base in Icecrown with an inn, stables and a flight master. Baron Sliver directs the Ebon Blade fight against the Scourge here, while Duke Lankral leads the campaign against the vrykul of Jotunheim. Vaelen the Flayed returns to recover captured death knights, and vault geists, morbid carcasses and shadow cultists roam the grounds.

You are in Jotunheim, the ancestral home of the vrykul, where Ebon Blade death knights are held in cages. Vrykul spear-sisters, warriors and proto-drakes patrol the land, and sleeping Mjordin are kept in the Halls of the Ancestors. A spirit healer is here.

You are in Savage Ledge, a ledge in Jotunheim where vrykul contenders spar and fight for a place in the Lich King's service. Efrem the Faithful, a former Scarlet Onslaught member, and the contender Sigrid Iceborn meet all who challenge them. Mjordin combatants and Jotunheim warriors are the main danger here.

You are in The Argent Vanguard, the Argent Crusade's base in Icecrown, with a flight master, repairs, a spirit healer and a vendor. Highlord Tirion Fordring leads the crusade's struggle against the Lich King, and Crusade Commander Entari and Siegemaster Fezzik hold the defenses. Forgotten Depths nerubians pour through the breach, and Scourge frost wyrms and Carrion Fleshstrippers attack the walls.
You are in Ironwall Dam in Icecrown, where pustulent horrors are a danger.

You are in the Valley of Echoes, a valley in Icecrown just outside the Breach. The Ebon Watcher, a former servant of the Lich King, gives aid to the Argent Crusade, and Father Gustav and Crusade Architect Silas plan a fortress called Justice Keep on the site of Scourgeholme. Horde emblem quartermasters trade here, and Forgotten Depths nerubians and carrion fleshstrippers roam the valley.

You are in The Breach, the passage between the Valley of Echoes and Scourgeholme in Icecrown. Reanimated crusaders and wrathstrike gargoyles lurk here. A crusader rescued from Scourgeholme warns that an attack is coming.

You are in Scourgeholme, the first Scourge encampment in Icecrown, reached through the Breach. Forgotten Depths high priests and reanimated crusaders fill its tiers, and the Scourge hold captured Argent crusaders as living shields. Salranax the Flesh Render lords over the first tier, and Underking Talonox holds court at the Pit of Fiends.

You are in The Broken Front, a battlefield in Icecrown where wounded Horde and Alliance soldiers lie among the fighting. Dying soldiers of both sides beg for mercy. Risen Alliance soldiers, icy ghouls and vicious geists fight here.

You are in Mord'rethar: The Death Gate in Icecrown, where skeletal craftsmen, icy ghouls and pustulent horrors wander. Slain Alliance soldiers lie here, and risen Alliance soldiers, vicious geists and plagued fiends are the dangers.

You are in The Bombardment, a part of Icecrown where Kor'kron troops push toward the gates of Ymirheim under Ground Commander Xutjja. Gargoyle ambushers, skeletal footsoldiers and stitched brutes make the approach dangerous, and scourge war machines are among the dangers. A Horde airship stops here.

You are in Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate, a part of Icecrown where Horde and Alliance engineers fly bombers against the Scourge. Fringe Engineer Tezzla drives the Horde effort, and Kibli Killohertz directs Alliance bombing runs. Cult researchers, bitter initiates and cult blackguards are the main dangers, with shadow channelers and vile torturers.

You are in Ymirheim, a vrykul city in Icecrown where Frazzle Geargrinder and Blast Thunderbomb are locked in a jumpbot contest over engineering pride. Carrion hunters, Ymirheim chosen warriors and spear guns are the dangers. Repairs, a spirit healer and a vendor are here.

You are in The Conflagration, a part of Icecrown where an Orgrim's Hammer scout is posted. Skeletal reavers, ravaged ghouls and vargul wanderers roam here, with scourge soulbinders, scourge deathchargers and a frostbrood matriarch among the dangers.

You are in Weeping Quarry, a saronite quarry in Icecrown where risen laborers and restless lookouts work. Hungering plaguehounds prowl the base, and Scourge containment crystals are scattered through it.

You are in Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate, a gate in Icecrown where cultist shard watchers and harbingers of horror are the main dangers, with corp'rethar guardians, necrotic webspinners, bone guards and scourgebeak fleshrippers.

You are in The Court of Bones, a court in Icecrown where boneguard footmen, scouts and commanders fight, with skeletal archmages and cruel overseers. Matthias Lehner tells of the prince's near-fatal battle here and says a bloodstained stone on the floor shows what happened. Argent peacekeepers and Crusader Maran are among the Argent forces.
You are in Malykriss: The Vile Hold, a hold in Icecrown where death knight initiates, skeletal runesmiths and a lumbering atrocity are the dangers.

You are in the Cathedral of Darkness, a cathedral in Icecrown where Highlord Tirion Fordring urges his allies to keep their heads down, follow his lead and stand ready against the Lich King. Chosen zealots, cultist acolytes and glacial bonelords are the dangers, and a disguised crusader fights beside Tirion's defenders.

You are in Icecrown Citadel, a fortress in Icecrown where the Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers each work to restore the blade Quel'Delar. Caladis Brightspear leads the Covenant's effort and Myralion Sunblaze the Sunreavers'. Below the citadel, Sergeant Kregga and Captain Kendall lead rival assaults with saronite bombs. Hulking horrors, boneguards and faceless lurkers are the dangers.

You are in Icecrown Glacier, open ice in Icecrown where converted heroes are the most common danger. Scourge banner-bearers, vargul wanderers, ravaged ghouls, scourge soulbinders and skeletal reavers are also here.

You are in Valhalas, the vrykul battle pit of Icecrown, where Geirrvif the val'kyr arranges the bouts. Gjonner the Merciless, a vrykul death knight, oversees them and calls even hard-won victories unimpressive. Njorndar spear-sisters, Jotunheim warriors and Mjordin water magi fight in the ring.

You are in Njorndar Village, a village in Icecrown that neither the Alliance nor the Horde holds. The Bone Witch, a banshee who inhabits a vrykul, lives here and sends people against the vrykul of Jotunheim. Jotunheim warriors, Mjordin water magi and Njorndar spear-sisters roam the land around it.

You are in The Fleshwerks, a Scourge works in Icecrown where the dead are stitched into abominations. Ghouls, skeletal constructors and corpulent horrors work and fight here. Margrave Dhakar of the Ebon Blade rallies his knights here, and Father Kamaros, a Light-devoted survivor, is still trapped among the Scourge.

You are in Sindragosa's Fall, a place in Icecrown where a whole brood of blue dragons fell. Matthias Lehner says the Lich King is raising the fallen blue dragons. Frostbrood whelps, wyrm reanimators and cultist corrupters roam here, and High Thane Jorfus is among the vrykul. An Alliance airship stops here.

You are in The Valley of Lost Hope, a valley in Icecrown where Alliance troops push toward Ymirheim. Ground Commander Koup leads them, and repeated vrykul ambushes have cost him men. Scourge war machines, frostskull magi and decomposed ghouls roam the valley.

You are in The Valley of Fallen Heroes, a valley in Icecrown where the fallen are turned against the living. Converted heroes, fallen heroes' spirits and Scourge converters roam it, and restless lookouts keep watch.

You are in Crusaders' Pinnacle, a stronghold in Icecrown where the Argent Crusade brings its wounded. Highlord Tirion Fordring is here, working to save Crusader Bridenbrad from undeath. Warlord Hork Strongbrow and Marshal Ivalius lie dying here after the Broken Front, and the dragonkin Penumbrius offers flights.

You are in Blackwatch, a base in Icecrown where Darkrider Arly pushes for intelligence to disrupt the Fleshwerks. Crusader Olakin Sainrith investigates the Scourge's use of metal and wants the fallen dead burned. Vile creepers lurk nearby.

You are in the Silent Vigil, a place in northeast Icecrown where the plague-stricken crusader Bridenbrad waits for death. He refuses to return to safety for fear of exposing others, and he remains grateful to those who help. A spirit healer here offers a return to life, though it may not yet be the traveler's time.

You are in Rise of Suffering, an Ebon Blade post in Icecrown. Vereth the Cunning, an Ebon Blade agent, directs the fight against death knights still loyal to Arthas at Malykriss. His controlled lithe stalkers scout the citadel and provoke fights among its undead workforce.

You are in the First Legion Forward Camp, a Lordaeron camp in Icecrown where soldiers hold the line against undead assaults. Matthias Lehner says he saw the prince raise the undead, and that fighting the Scourge only swells its ranks. Decomposed ghouls and frostskull magi press the camp.

You are in the Argent Tournament Grounds, a tourney camp in Icecrown where valiants from Stormwind, Ironforge, Orgrimmar and other cities train. Marshal Jacob Alerius, Stormwind's grand champion, welcomes recruits, and Mokra the Skullcrusher does the same for Orgrimmar. Sir Marcus Barlowe, master of arms, drills valiants against converted heroes. Hungry jormungar roam its edges.

You are in The Ring of Champions, a practice ring at the Argent Tournament in Icecrown. Squire Cavin summons knights here for practice bouts. Champions from Stormwind, Gnomeregan and Orgrimmar wait to be challenged, and facing one is no simple task.

You are in The Aspirants' Ring, a tournament ring in Icecrown. Squire David (n33447) asks challengers whether they are ready to fight a valiant of the Argent Crusade, and says he will call forth a member once they are.

You are in The Argent Valiants' Ring, a tournament ring in Icecrown where Horde and Alliance valiants of the Argent Tournament gather. Squire Danny (n33518) summons an Argent Champion as the opponent of any competitor who chooses to fight.

You are in The Alliance Valiants' Ring, a tournament ring in Icecrown. Darnassus, Stormwind, Exodar and Ironforge valiants stand here to challenge others to a joust, warning that the contest is no simple task and wishing a beaten challenger better luck next time.

You are in The Horde Valiants' Ring, a tournament ring in Icecrown where valiants from Sen'jin, Orgrimmar, Silvermoon, Thunder Bluff and Undercity call challengers to prepare for a demanding match. They warn that a valiant is no simple task, and the Undercity valiant wishes a defeated opponent better luck another time.

You are in Quel'Delar's Rest, a place in Icecrown where the Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers both work to restore Quel'Delar, a broken dragonforged blade. Caladis Brightspear (n36624) vows the Covenant will see it restored, while Myralion Sunblaze (n36642) insists the Sunreavers must. A Silver Covenant sentinel (n36656) turns away visitors it takes for minions of the Lich King.

You are in Deathspeaker's Watch, a place in Icecrown held by the Cult of the Damned. Dark Zealots (c34728) and Dark Ritualists (c34734) haunt the grounds, and Deathspeaker Kharos (c34808) leads them. Captive aspirants are kept here, and Kul the Reckless (n34956) is among the prisoners.
